rows.author: C066
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECRIMINALIZING CERTAIN OFFENSES IN THE REVISED PENAL CODE
rows.abstract: Offenses Decriminalized. - The following offenses under the Revised Penal Code are hereby decriminalized: (a) Vagrants as defined in Art. 202. (b) Pre-mature marriage as defined in Art. 351. (c) Abandonment of minor by person entrusted with his custody; indifference of parents as defined in Art. 277.  The enactment of the proposed bill also answers one of the causes of a prolonged disposition of criminal offenses thereby contributing to the over clogging of our courts which suppose crimes are but products of omissions, negligence and without necessarily disturbing the peace and order of our community.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-09-25

rows.author: C066
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVEN THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Aside from yielding gains and good results, the seven (7) years of the Local Government Code implementation have also brought to light some gaps, inconsistencies , rigidities, weaknesses, or simple oversights in the code itself.  The pastseven years have also occasioned changes in LGU conditions that call for adjustment in the policies that the Code provides.  All these require looking again at the Code proposing amendments where necessary. >The proposed amendments seek to address these concerns:  (1) RELATIONS AND PRINCIPLES (2) DEVOLUTION/POWE RS AND FUNCTIONS (3) REVENUE SOURCES AND FISCAL MANAGEMENT (4) STRUCTURES AND SYSTEMS (5) POPULAR PARTICIPATION
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-09-25

rows.abstract: "The Retirement Law of the National Prosecution Service". This Act shall apply to Prosecutors, Provincial/City Fiscals and their Assistants who are appointed or designated by the President under Presidential Decree No. 1275, as amended. >Rationale:Existing laws DO NOT adequately provide for the retirement of members of the National Prosecution Service despite their roles as the partner of the Judiciary in the dispensation of justice and as an indispensable component of our criminal justice system, being at the forefront in the investigation and prosecution of criminal cases. Existing economic conditions have rendered inadequate benefits under the existing retirement laws thus necessitating an expanded and improved retirement law and the ggrant of other benefits to prosecutors/fis cals commensurate to the risks and hazards of their work.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-09-25

rows.abstract: "Department of Housing Act of 2001". rows.title_full: AN ACT ELEVATING THE PHILIPPINE NORMAL UNIVERSITY TO BECOME THE COUNTRY'S NATIONAL UNIVERSITY FOR TEACHER EDUCATION, ESTABLISHING A SYSTEM OF NATIONAL TEACHER TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The honor and distinction of a national university for teacher education is conferred on the Philippine Normal University (PNU) in recognition of its progressive leadership in the field of teacher education. Since its inception of September 1, 1901, the university remains the only university in the country offering no other program but the teacher education program.  The PNU has consistently proven the quality of excellence of its teacher education programs by the significant publications and research work of the faculty; the national and international distinctions and honor conferred on its faculty and alumni; and its outstanding leadership in promoting teacher education reforms in the country.

rows.abstract: This bill states that NO BAIL shall be granted for violations of the Dangerous Drugs Law involving the following quantities: >1. 4 grams or more of opium; 2. 4 grams or more of morphine; 3. 5 grams or more of shabu or methylamphetami ne hydrochloride; 4. 4 grams of heroine; 5. 30 grams or more of Indian hemp or marijuana; 6. 5 grams or more of resin or marijuana resin oil; 7. 4 grams or more of cocaine or cocaine hydrochloride; or 8. In the case of other dangerous drugs, the quantity of which is far beyond therapeutic requirements, as determined and promulgated by the Dangerous Drugs Board, after consultation/he arings conducted for the purpose.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PRESERVE THE BUILT HERITAGE AND CULTURAL LANDSCAPES OF THE COUNTRY, PROVIDING FOR THE CREATION OF THE NATIONAL LANDMARKS COUNCIL AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Built Heritage Conservation Act of 2001". Built heritage represents a facet of Philippine culture that blends artistic principles with practical purpose.  This law recognizes the immediate need to protect rapidly vanishing structure or cultural landscapes pursuant to the 1987 Constitution which provides that all othe country's artistic and historic wealth constitutes the cultural treasure of the nation and shall be under the protection of the State which may regulate its disposition. >While recognizing the right of individual ownership, this law seeks to recognize a greater communal right and strives to attain a balance between both needs, to attain the greater good. A NATIONAL LANDMARKS COUNCIL is hereby created for this purpose.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2001-09-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF AN ORGANIC FARMING TRAINING AND PRODUCTION FACILITY IN EVERY AGRICULTURAL BARANGAY IN THE COUNTRY AND ESTABLISHING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Organic farming is a traditional practice that our forefathers had known since precolonial era.  It is a farming system that is cost-free and environment-fri endly, a system we so badly need if we want to revitalize the sagging agricultural economy of the country. >This bill seeks to encourage our farmers to revert to that system in order to significantly cut on agricultural cost as well as to save the degenerating natural environment in the countryside.

rows.abstract: "Anti-Midnight Appointments and Transactions Act of 2001". This bill applies to all elective executive officials of Local Government Units including Governors, Vice-Governors, Mayors, Vice-Mayors, and Punong Barangays. >Ninety (90) days immediatelybefore the next regular elections and up to the end of their term, no local executive officials as mentioned above shall make appointments, except temporary appointments to executive positions when continued vacancies therein will prejudice public service or endanger public safety. rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING A MAGNA CARTA OF WOMEN IN RURAL DEVELOPMENT
rows.abstract: This Act shall cover all women be they adult or girl-child engaged in agricultural production, manufacturing and service sectors located in rural areas and still participate in agricultural works and/or food production, and/or women and girl-child in indigenous communities, and to the extent herein provided, the departments, offices, agencies, subdivisions or instrumentaliti es of the national government. rows.title_full: AN ACT CONSOLIDATING THE MAPPING FUNCTION AND BUDGET UNDER THE OFFICE OF THE NATIONAL MAPPING AND RESOURCE INFORMATION AUTHORITY (NAMRIA)
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to consolidate the mapping budget of various departments of the government and centralizing such function under the office of the National Mapping and Resources Information Authority (NAMRIA). It has been observed, however, that there are other government agencies which still do their own mapping service resulting to duplication of efforts and costs.  In consonance with Executive Order No. 192, it is proposed that mapping work and the budget therefor be centralized for a more efficient and effective geographic information service, considering that NAMRIA is well equipped to do the job.

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE INCLUSION OF PSYCHIATRY IN THE MEDICAL BOARD EXAMINATIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED TWENTY-THREE HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-TWO, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE MEDICAL ACT OF 1959
rows.abstract: Rationale: The quality of a person's life is not only determined and enhanced by physical health but more so by mental and emotional stability.  It is so easy to forget that the diseases of the mind are often more virulent and have greater impact onthe lives of people than the diseases of the body. Furthermore, soundness of body requires mental and emotional equilibrium. Mental health not only enhances the physical well-being of people,  it assures their place as productive members of societyand permits them to make informed and intelligent decisions to be able to live and experience life to the fullest. > The inclusion of psychiatry as a medical board subject will not only increase the chances that psychiatry be recognized as a significcant medical discipline and elevated to its rightful place in the medical community. More importantly, it is an assurance that patients suffering from various forms of mental, behavioral and emotional problems will be handled by doctors who may not b
rows.status: Substituted by HB04729

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE PENALTY IMPOSED AGAINST POLLUTERS OF NAVIGABLE WATERS BY AMENDING SECTION 7 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 979 PROVIDING FOR THE REVISION OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 600 GOVERNING MARINE POLLUTION
rows.abstract: Rationale: Presidential Decree No. 979 states that it is the policy of the state to prevent and control the pollution of seas by the dropping of wastes and other matter which create hazards to human health, harm living resources and marine life, damage amenities, or interfere with the legitimate uses of the sea within the territorial jurisdiction of the Philippines. Section 7 of Presidential Decree No. 979 is hereby amended to read as follows: >Section 7. Penalties for Violations. - Any personwho violates Section 4 of this Decree or any regulations prescribed in pursuance thereof, shall be liable for a fine of not less than [Two hundred pesos nor more than Ten thousand pesos] FIVE MILLION PESOS or by imprisonement of not less than [thirtyy days] EIGHT YEARS AND ONE DAY nor more than [one year] TWELVE YEARS or both such fine and imprisonment, for each offense, without prejudice to the civil liability of the offender in accordance with existing laws.

rows.abstract: "Philippine Coast Guard Law of 2001". The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) is hereby established as a distinct, armed, and uniformed commissioned service attached to the Department of Transportation and Communications hereinafter referred to as the "DOTC". As provided for in this bill-- >1. PCG will have the ability to pursue programs and projects in coordination with the private sector and foreign financing agencies and institutions for its development. 2. The PCG would create a more effective policy and program coordination and implementation of concerns affecting the maritime industry and maritime society. 3. It would enhance efficiency in the delivery of public service to the maritime sector. 4. Develop and promulgate a coordinated and welll-structured maritime program and eliminate fragmentation, overlapping and duplication of maritime safety functions.

rows.author: D034
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING AN ANTI-ILLEGAL RECRUITMENT CENTER IN EVERY DISTRICT NATIONWIDE, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The proposed ANTI-ILLEGAL RECRUITMENT CENTER is tasked to: a) disseminate information to job seekers or "would ne OFWs" on acts of illegal recruitment and placement; b) disseminate list of license recruitment/pla cement agencies in every municipalities and all barangays by utilizing all and every means available; c) receive complaints of victims of illegal recruitment and placement; d) submit reports and coordinate with the national offices of the Department of Labor and Employment, PhilippineOverseas Employment Administration, National Labor Relations Commission and the Department of Justice on cases of illegal recruitment and placement, etc.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-09-25
